en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the injustices of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the country's national bird and is critically endangered.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines serves as the highest tribunal and interprets the laws under the judicial branch.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed an improvised bamboo incubator to provide medical care for infants in rural Philippine areas.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The Philippine Constitution guarantees every citizen the right to free and basic public education from elementary through high school.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a vibrant street dance mimicking a river's water current.
Filipino, which is primarily based on Tagalog, serves as the national language alongside English as an official language.
National Artist for Sculpture Napoleon Abueva created the iconic Nine Muses statue located at the University of the Philippines.
